captions: Chapter three. The SMILE investor.
If Damani is silence, our next winner is the

opposite — loud, joyful, and completely open about
how
he does it.
And his own life is the real version of
the rags-to-riches dream the fakes only imitate.

Vijay Kedia came to Mumbai around nineteen ninety
with
very little, after his family business faltered.
He learned the market the slow, painful way —

and built a disclosed portfolio worth roughly one
thousand

crore rupees today, across about twenty-one
companies.
His method even has a name — SMILE.

Small in size. Medium in experience. Large in
aspiration.
Extra-large in market potential.
In plain terms: he buys tiny companies with room
to become big ones — names like Tejas Networks,
Atul Auto, Cera Sanitaryware — and then he does
the hardest thing in investing.
He waits. Five years. Ten years.
Even now he's still adding — a fresh stake
in Eimco Elecon this June.
His edge isn't a secret indicator. It's conviction —
and a decade of holding through the noise.
Kedia likes to say the market rewards courage but
punishes greed.
Bulls make money. Bears make money. But pigs —
the greedy ones chasing every hot tip — get
slaughtered.
Every winner in this video, in their own way,
learned to sit still.
That's the muscle the fakes never show you building.
